intro: Foundations of International Law. Unit twelve: international responsibility, part one — the responsibility of states.

slides.2: Why responsibility is the test of a legal order. A legal subject is the holder of rights and obligations; violating an obligation triggers responsibility, that is, legal consequences — sanctions in the sense of punishment, a duty to make reparation, or other duties such as abstaining from certain conduct. And here is the point this whole course keeps returning to: responsibility is the test of a legal system's efficiency, because enforcement and effect require a centralised organ — and international law has only very basic approaches to that.
